retained_skill: Design and validate an rsyslog configuration that receives and forwards syslog over TLS, preserves facility/severity metadata, and prevents forwarding loops.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts first went wrong while bringing up rsyslog TLS. Seven repeatedly hit certificate access failures at the required /etc/rsyslog/certs path, while five began with missing-driver or RainerScript configuration errors; 11 exhausted context while repeatedly rewriting and validating rsyslog configuration, and only four reached the analyzer.
change: Structural help in the environment prepares the self-signed CA and localhost server certificate/key before the episode at the required location and stages copies in rsyslog's readable configuration tree. This removes certificate generation and makes the repeated inaccessible-path debugging a direct response to rsyslog's original error signal while preserving the student's full decision about the TLS listener, TLS forwarding, metadata format, and loop prevention.
restore: A later hardening can remove the prepared and staged certificates so the student must generate certificates and diagnose the certificate-path confinement before configuring TLS.
prediction: Attempts currently respond to certificate access or module errors by repeatedly changing permissions, paths, and complete rsyslog configurations. Prepared readable certificates let them proceed directly from rsyslog validation errors to correcting TLS configuration and then complete the analyzer/web stages; this is refuted if the next 12 attempts still spend most turns on certificate paths or none reaches working TLS forwarding.
